representation.name: Disassembler reconstruct (Logan haplotypes -> codon MSA)
representation.description: From a list of SRA accessions (e.g. kmindex hit accessions), stream each run's Logan unitig graph, walk out the target gene's coding haplotypes, and build a reference-guided codon MSA + FastTree. Composite of disassembler walker -> (sieve) -> msa. Requires outbound network to logan-pub.s3.amazonaws.com.
representation.shell_command:
ln -s '$(inputs.reference.path)' k13_ref.fasta && \
disassembler reconstruct \
  -l '$(inputs.accessions.path)' \
  -q k13_ref.fasta \
  --msa-reference k13_ref.fasta \
  -o out \
  -w $(inputs.workers) \
  --max-size-mb 512 \
  --emit-snv-table \
  --mafft-threads $(inputs.workers) \
  -- --scratch-dir . -t 1 && \
touch out/reconstructed.fasta out/alt_haplotypes.fasta out/snvs.tsv \
  out/k13_ref_codon_msa.fasta out/k13_ref_fasttree.nwk out/summary.json

help.content:
Accessions file: one SRA run accession per line (ERR/SRR/DRR). Reference:
in-frame coding-sequence FASTA used both as the walker anchor and the MSA
reference. The `--scratch-dir .` override is required because /dev/shm is
only ~64 MB inside a default job container; `-t 1` pins GraphAligner to a
single thread for reproducibility (see disassembler docs/walker.md).
NOTE: each accession streams a ~10-50 MB compressed unitig object over the
network - run hundreds of accessions per job, not tens of thousands.
